source_text: Οὐδὲν γὰρ οὕτω τὰς Ἐκκλησίας λυμαίνεται, ὡς τοῦτο τὸ νόσημα· καὶ καθάπερ σῶμα μὴ μετὰ ἀκριβείας συνδεδεμένον τῇ τῶν νευρῶν περιβολῇ, πολλὰς τίκτει τὰς ἀῤῥωστίας, καὶ ἀβίωτον ποιεῖ τὸν βίον· οὕτω καὶ Ἐκκλησία, μὴ σφοδρᾷ καὶ ἀῤῥαγεῖ τῇ τῆς ἀγάπης ἁλύσει περιβεβλημένη, μυρίους τίκτει πολέμους, καὶ τὴν ὀργὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ αὔξει, καὶ πολλῶν πειρασμῶν γίνεται ὑπόθεσις. Ἵνα οὖν μὴ ταῦτα συμβαίνῃ, μηδὲ τὸν Θεὸν παροξύνωμεν, καὶ τὰ ἡμέτερα ἐπαυξήσωμεν κακὰ, καὶ τὴν κόλασιν ἀπαραίτητον παρασκευάζωμεν, καὶ πολλῆς ἀηδίας πληρῶμεν τὴν ζωὴν τὴν ἡμετέραν, πρὸς εὐφημίαν τὴν γλῶτταν μεταθέντες, τὸν ἑαυτῶν καθ' ἑκάστην ἡμέραν περιεργαζώμεθα βίον, καὶ τὴν ἑτέρων ζωὴν τῷ τὰ ἀπόῤῥητα μετὰ ἀκριβείας εἰδότι κρίνειν ἐπιτρέψαντες, αὐτοὶ τὰ ἑαυτῶν ἁμαρτήματα κρίνωμεν. Οὕτω γὰρ καὶ τὸ τῆς γεέννης δυνησόμεθα διαφυγεῖν πῦρ. Ὥσπερ γὰρ οἱ τὰ ἀλλότρια πολυπραγμονοῦντες κακὰ, τῶν οἰκείων οὐδένα ποιοῦνται λόγον· οὕτως οἱ δεδοικότες εἰς τὸν ἑτέρων παρακύψαι βίον, πολλὴν ἑαυτοῖς τῶν πεπλημμελημένων ποιήσονται τὴν φροντίδα· οἱ δὲ τὰ ἑαυτῶν ἀναλογιζόμενοι κακὰ, καὶ ταῦτα καθ' ἑκάστην κρίνοντες τὴν ἡμέραν, καὶ δίκας ἑαυτοὺς ἀπαιτοῦντες, ἥμερον ἕξουσι τότε τὸν δικαστήν. Καὶ τοῦτο ὁ Παῦλος δηλῶν ἔλεγεν· Εἰ γὰρ ἑαυτοὺς ἐκρίνομεν, οὐκ ἂν ἐκρινόμεθα ὑπὸ Κυρίου, Ἵν' οὖν διαφύγωμεν τὴν ψῆφον ἐκείνην, πάντα τὰ ἄλλα ἀφέντες, περιεργαζώμεθα τὴν ἑαυτῶν ζωὴν, καὶ κολάζωμεν τὸν λογισμὸν τὸν ἁμαρτάνειν ἀναπείθοντα, καὶ κατανύττωμεν τὸ συνειδὸς, καὶ λόγον ἑαυτοὺς ἀπαιτῶμεν τῶν πεπραγμένων ἡμῖν. Οὕτω γὰρ δυνησόμεθα κοῦφον τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ποιήσαντες τὸ φορτίον, συγγνώμης ἀπολαῦσαι πολλῆς, καὶ τὸν παρόντα βίον μεθ' ἡδονῆς διάγειν, καὶ τῶν μελ λόντων ἐπιτυχεῖν ἀγαθῶν, χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι' οὗ καὶ μεθ' οὗ τῷ Πατρὶ δόξα, ἅμα τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
orientation: Chrysostom is concluding the homily, warning that slander against spiritual fathers is a disease that harms the churches, and urging self-examination instead of judging others.
pass_a_gloss: For nothing so harms the churches as this disease; and just as a body not bound together with precision by the wrapping of the sinews produces many sicknesses and makes life unlivable, so also a church not wrapped in the strong and unbreakable chain of love produces countless wars, and increases the wrath of God, and becomes an occasion of many trials. In order therefore that these things may not happen, and that we may not provoke God, and may not increase our own evils, and may not prepare an inexorable punishment, and may not fill our life with much unpleasantness, having turned the tongue toward good speech, let us busy ourselves with our own life each day, and having entrusted the life of others to the one who knows the secrets with precision to judge, let us ourselves judge our own sins. For thus we shall be able to escape the fire of Gehenna. For just as those who busy themselves with the evils of others make no account of their own, so those who fear to pry into the life of others will make much care for themselves of their transgressions; and those who reckon up their own evils, and judge these each day, and demand penalties of themselves, will have the judge gentle then. And Paul making this clear said: For if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged by the Lord. In order therefore that we may escape that verdict, having let go all other things, let us busy ourselves with our own life, and let us punish the reasoning that persuades to sin, and let us prick the conscience, and let us demand of ourselves an account of the things done by us. For thus, having made the burden of our sins light, we shall be able to enjoy much pardon, and to pass the present life with pleasure, and to attain the good things to come, by the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom and with whom to the Father be glory, together with the Holy Spirit, unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: The verb means to ruin or damage; 'harms' fits the medical metaphor of disease afflicting the churches.
The slander is presented as a sickness; 'disease' preserves the medical imagery.
The image is of a chain binding the church together; 'unbreakable' renders the alpha-privative adjective literally.
The verb means to occupy oneself with something as a busybody or with excessive care; here it is redirected positively to one's own life.

choices.why: The verb means to pierce or sting; 'prick' preserves the physical metaphor of compunction.

pass_b_english: For nothing harms the churches as much as this disease. Just as a body not tightly bound by its network of sinews produces many sicknesses and makes life unlivable, so too a church not wrapped in the strong, unbreakable chain of love produces countless wars, increases the wrath of God, and becomes the occasion of many trials. So that these things may not happen, and so that we may not provoke God, increase our own evils, prepare an inexorable punishment for ourselves, and fill our life with much unpleasantness, let us turn our tongue to good speech, let us busy ourselves with our own life each day, and, entrusting the judgment of others' lives to the One who knows secrets with precision, let us judge our own sins. For in this way we will be able to escape the fire of Gehenna. Just as those who meddle in others' evils pay no attention to their own, so those who fear to pry into another's life will take great care of their own offenses. And those who reckon up their own evils, judging them each day and demanding an accounting from themselves, will find the Judge gentle at that time. Paul made this clear when he said, "For if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged by the Lord" (1 Corinthians 11:31). So that we may escape that verdict, let us leave everything else aside, busy ourselves with our own life, punish the reasoning that persuades us to sin, prick the conscience, and demand an accounting from ourselves for what we have done. For in this way, having made the burden of our sins light, we will be able to enjoy much forgiveness, pass through this present life with pleasure, and attain the good things to come, by the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom and with whom glory be to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, to the ages of ages. Amen.
